article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Morning Brief
article.dek: A quiet Saturday morning: Friday's clearances for Lamar Jackson and Saquon Barkley still stand, the morning cards are unchanged, and Sunday's slate is the one to set up.

items.headline: Lead: A quiet Saturday morning — Friday's clearances stand, and Sunday is the slate
paragraphs: No new injury or quarterback news turned up Saturday morning. Friday's final designations still stand: Lamar Jackson is cleared to return for Baltimore at Buffalo, and Saquon Barkley is cleared for Philadelphia at Washington.
There are no NFL games today. Thursday's Carolina at Green Bay game is already played, and the rest of Week 8 kicks off Sunday. Nothing today needs a rushed decision.
Use the quiet day to look at Sunday's cards in the app. The next real news comes with the inactive lists about 90 minutes before each Sunday kickoff.
items.takeaway: Jackson and Barkley are both cleared, no new news Saturday morning, and the slate starts Sunday.

items.headline: Injury roundup: the outs and questionables to carry into Sunday
paragraphs: The outs from Friday's final reports: Philadelphia is without DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey and Jonathan Jones. Washington is without starting defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw. Baltimore is without Vega Ioane and Jaylinn Hawkins.
The questionables to watch: Buffalo's DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid, Philadelphia's Jakorian Bennett, and Washington's Daron Payne, John Bates, Treylon Burks and Jer'Zhan Newton.
Questionable does not mean out. The inactive lists about 90 minutes before kickoff are the next real update — check them before you lock anything in on those games.
items.takeaway: The returns are the headline; the outs and questionables above are what the inactive lists will settle Sunday.

items.headline: Weather: no games Saturday, so Sunday's outdoor check comes Sunday morning
paragraphs: With no games today, there is no kickoff weather to report this morning.
Sunday's outdoor games get their final weather check in the Sunday morning brief. Weather is reported as fact, not as a reason to bet a total one way or the other.
items.takeaway: No games Saturday; Sunday's outdoor games get their final weather check Sunday morning.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Morning cards: Hit Rate, Balanced and Value all hold
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the Los Angeles Rams moneyline at -278 at DraftKings, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET against the Chargers. It is the pick the app rates most likely to win, with a model probability of 0.649. Remember the app's own tutorial: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
Balanced is Baltimore +3 at -104 at FanDuel, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET at Buffalo. It is a strong pick without paying too much — the middle ground, and a good starting point for a new bettor.
Value is Chicago +3 at -105 at DraftKings, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET at Seattle. Value is always the model's +EV play. The app rates it at a model probability of 0.506 with medium reliability.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate: Rams moneyline -278. Balanced: Baltimore +3 -104 at FanDuel. Value: Chicago +3 -105 at DraftKings.

items.headline: A card that holds still means checking your own price
paragraphs: The cards above are priced at DraftKings and FanDuel. If your book is neither, the card price is not your price.

Tap Check in the app, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here.
items.takeaway: Your book's price is the one that matters — run it through Check and let that verdict decide.

items.headline: Learn the Game: what a push is
paragraphs: A push is a tie against the spread. It is neither a win nor a loss, and your stake comes back.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you bet a team -3, and that team wins by exactly 3 points. The final margin lands exactly on the spread, so the bet pushes and your stake is returned.
That is why a line sitting on a common margin matters. A bet that pushes is not a bad beat and not a win — it is money back, and the card moves on.
items.takeaway: A push returns your stake, so a line sitting exactly on the final margin is neither a win nor a loss — know it before you judge a card.

items.headline: Morning board vs evening board: no card changes, only small price ticks
paragraphs: The morning board makes no card changes. Hit Rate, Balanced and Value are the same three picks as Friday evening.

The ticks: the Rams moneyline moved from -270 to -278 at DraftKings, with the play-through price moving from -275 to -283. Baltimore's DraftKings spread price ticked from -105 to -108, with the line still +3. FanDuel's Jacksonville spread moved from 10.5 to 9.5, and FanDuel prices ticked on the Chargers-Rams and Eagles-Commanders lines.

No line crossed a key number, and the app's morning refresh caught all of it. If your book shows something different from the prices above, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app re-evaluate it for you.
items.takeaway: No card changes overnight — the Rams price ticked to -278, Baltimore's spread price ticked to -108, and everything else is small.

items.headline: Saturday job: set Sunday up, and log everything honestly
paragraphs: There is one piece of information worth waiting for: the inactive lists, about 90 minutes before each Sunday kickoff, for the questionable names above. That is a real pending event with a set time.
Everything else is ready now. If your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet now — waiting for the Sunday rush lets the number drift the wrong way too, especially on big-name teams.

One more Saturday habit: settlement in the app is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too. A tracker that only holds winners is not a record, it is a highlight reel.
items.takeaway: Wait only for Sunday's inactive lists; otherwise bet when Check says bet — and log every result, winners and losers alike.

evidence.fact: Baltimore QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) carries no game designation on Friday's final injury report after full practices Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, and head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Friday Jackson will play Sunday at Buffalo. Baltimore ruled out RG Vega Ioane (knee) and S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee). No new Jackson news appeared Saturday morning.

Philadelphia RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was limited in Friday practice after missing Wednesday and Thursday, and carries no game designation for Sunday night at Washington. No new Barkley news appeared Saturday morning.

Friday's final reports: Philadelphia ruled out WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), LB Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), WR Britain Covey (knee) and CB Jonathan Jones (hamstring); CB Jakorian Bennett is questionable (knee). Washington ruled out starting DL Javon Kinlaw; DL Daron Payne (foot), TE John Bates, WR Treylon Burks and DL Jer'Zhan Newton are questionable. Buffalo listed WR DJ Moore and TE Dalton Kincaid questionable, among six Bills listed questionable.
